title: HeartbeatRequest
description: Periodic worker heartbeat (protocols.md §6): presence mode, installed vs loaded models, current queue subscriptions, and rolling stats. Also the poll point for updates.

loaded.description: Warm right now — enables model-affinity routing.

digests.description: Optional artifact → content digest, where the model server exposes it. Ability is pinned to an artifact (ADR 15), so a changed digest means a NEW artifact whose score must be re-measured rather than inherited.

load_s.description: Median seconds to bring a model up from cold on this node, measured by subtracting the generation the node's own `tps` accounts for from a cold job's wall time. Storage speed times model size, which no probe of either alone can predict. Omitted until measured — a node that has never observed a cold start has no load time, and 0 would claim it warms instantly. Absent on model servers that cannot report which models are resident, since coldness must be proven rather than assumed.

protocol_version.description: Queue-contract protocol version the worker speaks (skew gating, §7).

action_result.description: Outcome of the model-management action the previous heartbeat response issued. Closes the loop so the coordinator can mark the proposal applied or failed.

agent_version.description: The worker's build-stamped release version (semver-ish, e.g. 0.7.0). The coordinator judges FITNESS from this, not just protocol compatibility: a version can speak the contract correctly and still carry bugs that produce wrong results.

agent_flavour.description: Which worker implementation this is, and therefore which release artifact it can actually EXECUTE: 'dotnet' selects a .NET runtime id (osx-arm64, linux-x64, …), 'python' selects the single platform-independent py3-none-any artifact. Deliberately an open string rather than an enum so a new worker language needs no contract change (the C# worker is a reference implementation, not a constraint — ADR 7). Absent ⇒ 'dotnet', the only implementation predating this field. The coordinator FAILS CLOSED: a flavour it has no artifact mapping for is offered no update at all, because handing a worker a binary it cannot run — or worse, one it would install over its own entrypoint — is far worse than leaving it on an old version.
